cross_axis_bounds.rule: --rows caps the proposals verified per round at rows - 1 (commands.c). A draft block or depth that another source of the row sets above that cap is clamped to it: the extra block positions cost time and verify nothing (r5c on TP4_PRO: depth 7 on rows 6 with arm 1 lost 10.2 % to r5s, rows 6 with arm 1 at depth 5, 232.3 -> 208.5 tok/s code C1). Bounds act on the final values, explicit ones included, and change only inserted knobs: an explicit --rows=6 keeps the clamp, --rows=8 lifts it; an explicit bounded knob is never altered and is validated as usual. A cap never lowers a knob below the least its parser takes (--draft_block 5, --draft_positions 1), also where the final speculation is off and the clamped draft knobs are inert, noted inactive (a raw --rows=1 --speculative=0 parses).

Sharded BATCH draft rows require draft layers (model_v41.c: batch_draft_rows with draft_shards needs draft_layers). Where the final --tp_draft_shards=1 and --batch_draft_rows are composed or given (TP4_EXL3 concurrency=multiple), an inserted --tp_draft_layers is raised to 1, the value every BATCH tuple ran with before the per-split tables. Bounds act on the final values: an explicit --tp_draft_shards=1 keeps the raise, --tp_draft_shards=0 or --batch_draft_rows=0 removes it; an explicit --tp_draft_layers is never altered and is validated as usual.

The draft's shards need the target head's (commands.c: --tp_draft_shards needs --tp_head_shards=1). TP4_EXL3's base inserts --tp_head_shards=1 and --tp_draft_shards=1, and an explicit knob replaces only its own key, so before this cap an explicit --tp_head_shards=0 left the inserted draft shards at 1 and the parser refused the command: where the final --tp_head_shards is 0, an inserted --tp_draft_shards is lowered to 0, and the explicit knob wins alone. An explicit --tp_draft_shards is never altered and is validated as usual.

This cap mirrors the draft-shards part of the parser's layers rule (commands.c: --tp_draft_layers needs TP4_EXL3 with the BF16 wire and --tp_draft_shards=1, on BATCH also --batch_draft_rows=1 and --batch_wide_head=1): where the final --tp_draft_shards is 0, given or lowered by the head-shards cap, an inserted --tp_draft_layers (focus=decode's, or the BATCH rows' raised one) is lowered to 0. No bound follows the rule's other parts, so an explicit --tp_wire_bf16=0 or, on BATCH, --batch_draft_rows=0 under focus=decode's layers, or --batch_wide_head=0 under any BATCH row's, is still refused. A bound reads its bounding knob after that knob's own bounds, one level (the generator refuses a longer chain), and a knob several bounds name takes the first, in declared order, that changes it, so the floor above no longer raises the layers once the head-shards cap has lowered the draft shards. An explicit --tp_draft_layers is never altered and is validated as usual.
